Build prompt

Rebuild this animation 1:1: Swiggy One BLCK's expiry banner - a skeuomorphic mini calendar in the home banner tears off its top page each time it appears, counting down the days left on the plan.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Swiggy home, dark purple header ("Diamond District", search bar) over a white category grid (FOOD DELIVERY, INSTAMART, DINEOUT, GIFTABLES, SCENES tiles). The banner: "one BLCK ends soon! ₹7,575 saved with your current plan. To keep saving, Extend Now" with a small square calendar widget at right showing the day count over "DAYS LEFT".

## Motion spec
Pattern: skeuomorphic calendar page-tear counting down days remaining.
- The banner slides in with the feed (300ms, ease-out) with the calendar showing the previous count.
- 600ms later the calendar's top page tears: the page's top edge lifts and curls down-and-over like paper (a 3D fold: rotateX from 0 to -160deg around the bottom binding over 500ms, ease-in) with a soft paper shadow sweeping the revealed page.
- The tearing page crumples slightly at the fold (skew +/-3deg near the end) and falls away with a fade (last 150ms).
- The revealed page shows the new count; the number pops 1.1 -> 1 (200ms) as the tear completes.
- At low counts (under 7 days) the calendar face tints warmer and the banner copy switches to the urgent variant.
- The rest of the home feed never reacts - the tear is a self-contained widget moment.

## Calibration
- The tear pivots on the calendar's binding edge - never a slide or a generic flip.
- Exactly one tear per banner appearance; re-appearing with an unchanged count shows no tear.

## Reduced motion
The count crossfades (250ms) without the page tear.

## Don't miss
- The count digits are large and centered with "DAYS LEFT" small beneath - the widget is readable at banner size.
- The falling page keeps the old number visible until it's gone - the before/after must both be seen.
